doc: The frozen I62 instrument: the rerun of I61's catalog with the defects I61's run found fixed (BUILD_PLAN §4 I22, whose kill criterion, threshold and exit it inherits, as I61 did). I61 ran its 242 mutants once (docs/iterations/I61.md, results/M2/mutation_i61/): its run showed five defects of the pipeline and one of the gate's rules (replaces.defects). I61's own rule: a defect found in a tool the rules keep unchanged is a Surprise, a fix needs a rerun of every mutant from scratch, and the first run's records are reported; and its gate allows no second attempt after a pass (harness_gate.passed). So the rerun is a new key. I62 keeps I61's 242 mutants, its diff sheet and every value computed from the pinned checkout byte for byte (in_scope, stillborn, sites, counts, edges, actions, predicted sets, structural classes, tce, the planted controls; mutants_sha256 and diff_sheet are I61's), keeps I61's panel verdicts (adjudication.panel: equivalence is a property of the mutant and the original program, which have not changed), and changes only what the defects touch: the replay semantics of a none value (replay.semantics), the errors clause (kill_criterion.errors: a failing set run is isolated law by law, a channel run that does not complete is retried), the i20_step channel and the trace replay on a mutant whose deployment reverts (channels.i20_step, replay.trace), the ledger and coverage of the header document (replaces.defects D3), the determinism of messages (reporting.determinism), and the gate (a control with a replay disagreement or a failed replay fails it; no check of the gate runs before its first attempt: harness_gate). Every I62 output has its own path; I61's records stay as its run wrote them. BUILD_PLAN names spec/M2/preregistration.json; a prereg commit may only add files under spec/M2/lib/ (holon/audit/prereg.py), hence the path. It is the only target-facing input of holon/mutate/ (HOLON_MUTATE_KEY I62, the default). Contract: the docstring of tests_m2/test_mutation_adequacy_i62.py. The values computed from the pinned checkout are I61's computation, unchanged (computation, pins); what ran before this prereg is listed (harness_gate.before_prereg).

first_run.status: reported as the first run, never edited (TestI61FirstRun): its rates, its 7 error outcomes and its Surprises stand in docs/iterations/I61.md; I62's rates supersede them as the measurement (reporting.metric)

replaces.rule: I61's contract (tests_m2/test_mutation_adequacy_i61.py, Rules): 'A defect found in them is a Surprise; a fix needs a rerun of every mutant from scratch, and the first run's records are reported.' Its gate (harness_gate.passed, `holon mutate gate`) stops at the first passing attempt, so a rerun with a fixed pipeline needs a new instrument, a new gate and new records: this key. The human chose it (the I61 PR's questions: a new key and rerun, the gate rule, the I20 harness, the header ledger bundle).
replaces.carried: I61's replaces (I60's findings and I22's, and what I61 did with them) still hold; I62 changes none of them. computation, pins, in_scope, stillborn, operators, operator_order, variant_order, cursor_pairs, counts, structural_counts, roles, law_sets, predicted, baseline, structural, projection, equivalence, duplicates, tce, survivor_classes, threshold, seed, target, strata, mutants_sha256, diff_sheet, the mutants and the planted controls are I61's, byte for byte.

defects.D1 (replay): a none value read as a call: replay.semantics says dec_go is None when validate() errs. holon.mutate.replay's claim evaluator read that value, None, as 'this call has not run yet', so a claim comparing it never finished ('the claim's evaluation did not finish'): the law became a replay disagreement with a replay error instead of being decided by its replay. In I61: six law entries, A001 (L_rt_go_v0, L_rt_go_v1, L_rt_go_v2), A058 (L_rt_go_v1) and the control C3 (L_rt_go_v1, L_rt_go_v2); no kill and no rate changed (each was killed through another law), A001's extraction_defect_detected was set by it alone, and C3's record showed it before any catalog mutant ran. Fix: replay.semantics (I62 sentence): a role whose value is none is a value, unequal to every some(...) value; a field of none, or a role called on none, is the model's undefined intermediate, no execution.
defects.D2 (channels, replay): a deployment that: I20's step harness and I15's trace harness deploy the target once per trace and fail the whole run when a deployment reverts. Five stratum-A mutants break Rollup's genesis import, so every trace's deployment reverts (A076 'batch header length too small', A098 'zero data hash', A100 and A101 'invalid versioned hash', A104 'zero state root'): their i20_step runs did not complete, and the SORT-width laws, which read the unit's own width values when its rollup document changed, were marked error: 5 error outcomes; their trace replays failed too. Fix: channels.i20_step and replay.trace run copies of the two harnesses' Solidity (replay/M2/mutation_i62/) that probe each trace's deployment from a snapshot that is then reverted; a trace whose deployment reverts runs no step. I20's and I15's own harnesses are not changed.
defects.D3 (ledger, coverage): a width law over: When a mutant makes the rollup document's store at a layout site non-narrowing (A027, A031: shl_width; A116, A120: shr_width, on the batch index), holon derive keeps that SORT-width site in the header layout document (facts spec/M2/facts/morph_header.extracted.json, no entry points), and holon run refused the law: no ledger bundle registers that document (holon.records.resolve_bundle), and past the ledger, no coverage entry can exist for it (holon coverage reports transitions documents only). The set's run failed and every law of the set was marked error: A116 and A120 ended in error (2 error outcomes); A027 and A031 were killed through other laws. Fix: spec/M2/ledger.json registers the header document's bundle, each of the document's four declared assumptions an entry introduced by every definition (a law over the document carries all four; no definition is assumption-free, so a derived document with a non-empty cone is refused), and holon.records.coverage_field gives a law over a document that is not a transitions document no coverage entry, as for hand-written facts. Neither changes a committed law, record status or output (gate M2 G1).
defects.D4 (errors): one failing law fails its w: kill_criterion.errors scopes errors to laws, but a failing `holon run --milestone M2` over the laws to decide marked every law of the set error (I61: the two width laws of A027, A031, A116, A120, whose sets held only them). Fix: kill_criterion.errors (I62 sentence): a set's run that fails twice is retried law by law.
defects.D5 (errors): channel runs were never ret: The channel functions report a run that does not complete as an incomplete entry instead of raising, so kill_criterion.errors' retry never applied to them. Fix: a channel run that does not complete is retried once (channels.retry).
defects.D6 (determinism): messages held timings: 9 I61 records were not byte-reproducible (AGENTS.md rule 7): their error messages held forge timings (A076, A098, A100, A101, A104) or runner scratch paths (A027, A031, A116, A120). Fix: reporting.determinism.
defects.D7 (gate): a control's replay disagreeme: I61's gate counted a control as passing when it was killed as expected, so C3 passed with two replay disagreements and two replay errors (D1) in its record. Fix: harness_gate.checks.controls (I62 sentence).
defects.D8 (gate): the first attempt came after: In I61 one build agent ran the gate's checks component by component before the gate's first attempt, so its first-attempt pass came after a rehearsal (docs/iterations/I61.md). Fix: harness_gate.rehearsal and harness_gate.before_prereg.

limitations: M1x laws are decided on I20's window view m1_view (the hand abstraction minus the requires no extracted check of the same action overlaps by span). No operator here adds or removes a check reach, so the view, and every M1x status, is carried by construction: 51 stratum-A mutants are abstraction-carried. A decision path that consumes extracted effects for the rollup laws does not exist at this pipeline.

M2 SORT-site laws are decided on the hand model; SORT-width laws on the extracted model, which has no Reach predicate, so they can only be UNKNOWN (docs/iterations/I20.md, Not done). No M2 law can move.

L_dom_hdr, L_par_hdr_v2 and L_par_hdr_ssvh are REFUTED at baseline: what they see is measured as masked obstructions, never as kills. Behind L_par_hdr_v2 even that is blind: enc_go_v1 writes version byte 1 where enc_sol writes 2, so every v2 candidate is false on the original code (S-A5).
The Solidity getters (mload_offset, shr_width) feed no projected op: the projection reads the stored Header fields, not how Rollup computed them. They are measured, not excluded.
Stratum B has no decision path: no adopted document reads node/types, the genesis encoder or batch_data. It is measured with no threshold.
The operator patterns are I22's (PutUint64 only, not PutUint16/32; a dropped length check whose body returns one of the I18 non-nil error forms), recomputed on the new scope.
Equivalence is over Rollup's public entry points: a library user that is not deployed (a mock) is out of it.

Whitepaper §9.5 lists 'wrong masks' among A1's misimplementations. No in-scope file of either stratum holds a literal bit mask (no Yul and(), no Go & with a constant, no 0xff literal outside comments; checked on the pinned bytes at the prereg), so no mask operator exists here; shl_width and shr_width are the nearest form. A mask operator is added when a scope holds a mask.
Rewrites are single-site and single-token (first-order mutants); interactions of two faults are not measured.

Unmutated sites (F-A5): the version byte has no literal offset in either language (BatchHeaderCodecV0.sol:133 mstore8(batchPtr, _version), :46 mload(batchPtr); batch_header.go:217 and :245 batchBytes[0] = .., :76 b[0]); the Go version comparisons of the dec_go getters (batch_header.go:116, :130, :143, :189) have no comparison operator here; the pointer bumps of the dataHash preimage (Rollup.sol:872 add(dataPtr, 8), :874 add(dataPtr, 2), :940 add(_ptr, 0x20)) are no operator's pattern; stratum-B copy and Put* calls with an explicit high bound (batch_cache.go:1833-1849, consensus_message.go:110-118, batch_data.go:107) match no Go pattern. The measured rate does not cover version-byte layout, Go comparison boundaries or pointer arithmetic.

K2 (a) is per law in name only for M0 (S-A2): law_sets.own_input hashes the whole projected document, so any change of the projection satisfies (a) for all 8 M0 laws; (b) and (c) carry the localization.

The two bvh_at site laws (S-A9) share (SORT, site, morph_rollup:bvh_at) in laws/M2/DERIVATION.json, so a re-derived one is 'new' (law_sets.matching needs exactly one match); its span is a hand-model definition, never K1-eligible. No effect while SORT-site laws are decided on the hand model.

enc_sol is replayed at the store level (replay.m0): the stored values are bound from the witness at the Header's widths, not computed by the entry function from its calldata and the parent header. A mutant of how the entry function computes a stored value (the batch index increment, the message count sum, the data hash) is invisible to M0 (projection_carried), as the projection already does not read it; witness values outside the entry function's parameter types (l1MessagePopped >= 2^16) are store-level executions, reported as function-level (equivalence.contradictions).
Premise-limited reachable mutants (F-A1): A148, A162, A165, A166, A167, A168 (structural.premise_limited).

I62 is a rerun: its predictions are I61's measured outcomes with the fixes' expected effects, made after I61's run and after the test units listed in harness_gate.before_prereg. They test whether the fixes do what they claim and nothing else, not the catalog's sensitivity afresh.
The equivalence verdicts are I61's panel's, carried (adjudication.panel). The panel judged the same sheet and pinned sources; it was blind to I61's results, which did not exist then.

The i20_step channel and the trace replay run the mutation copies of I20's step harness and I15's trace harness (replay/M2/mutation_i62/): the I20 and I15 tools themselves, and their committed outputs, are unchanged. On a tree whose every deployment reverts, the i20_step run compares no step (every corpus step differs) and every trace law holds on its replay (no step runs, so none panics).

A SORT-width law over the header document carries all four of the document's declared assumptions (replaces.defects D3): a conservative reading, since such a law is decided over the rollup document's model with an empty cone. Width laws are UNKNOWN in every case (the second limitation), so no kill reads them.

preconditions.order: Before any catalog mutant runs, all of: the catalog review (signed off) and then the adjudication (committed alone, after the review); the harness gate (passed; it needs neither the review nor the adjudication, and may run as soon as the build exists); the baseline (reproduced; it needs nothing before it); and I21's exit. Each of them descends from this prereg. The ledger bundle and coverage rule of replaces.defects D3, and the fixes of holon/mutate, are committed after this prereg and before the gate's first attempt (a prereg commit holds no code).
preconditions.i21_exit: I21's exit (BUILD_PLAN: zero open high-severity findings before I22): the tree of the records' pipeline_commit holds audit/rounds/M2/round2.json and no audit/M2_findings.jsonl line of severity 'high' and status 'open' (S-A6). It holds at pins.holon_commit.
preconditions.review: docs/iterations/I62_catalog_review.json, signed off, naming this instrument (adjudication.review)
preconditions.adjudication: spec/M2/equivalent_mutants_i62.json, complete, naming this instrument, catalog, sheet and review (adjudication.file), committed alone after the review
preconditions.gate: results/M2/mutation_i62/gate.json with passed true at the records' pipeline_commit (harness_gate), first committed before any catalog mutant's record
preconditions.baseline: results/M2/mutation_i62/baseline.json reproduces baseline.M0, baseline.M1x and baseline.M2 exactly, every committed spec/M2/facts/*.extracted.json (normalized sha256) and the committed projection; otherwise no catalog mutant runs and a projection or pipeline defect is reported, never a measurement (S-A7)
preconditions.refusal: `python -m holon mutate run` runs no catalog mutant (exit 2, nothing written) while a precondition is missing or fails: the review, the adjudication, a passed gate at the run's pipeline commit, a baseline record that reproduces, and I21's exit at the run's pipeline commit; --dry-run checks them all. --baseline-only and --control need none of them, and `holon mutate gate` needs neither the review nor the adjudication.

pins.why: The instrument reads the merged code and outputs at holon_commit (I20, I21, I40, I42 and I43 merged). files maps every committed artifact the computation, the harness gate and the preconditions read to its sha256 there; the extracted documents, laws, diagrams, coverage and bindings among them are byte-identical to I60's pins at 04e2293 (computation item 0). A later change of one of them is a note, never a reason to recompute the catalog: every record reports its predicted sets recomputed on the run's documents beside the frozen ones (predicted.recomputed). I62 keeps these pins (replaces.carried); i61_pipeline_commit is the first run's pipeline commit.

Every replacement keeps the file's line count. Ids per stratum (A001.., B001..) in operator_order, then in_scope.order, then offset, then variant_order.

threshold.source: docs/HUMAN_ANSWERS.md Q6 (0.80 of non-equivalent mutants in scope); docs/BUILD_PLAN.md §0.4
threshold.consequence: Stated before anything runs (S-A10, F-A2). structural_counts.A has 103 reachable mutants; 6 of them are premise-limited (structural.premise_limited), so at most 97 stratum-A mutants can be killed by a law that reads them. meets needs 5k >= 4n with n = 192 - e non-equivalent mutants: with k <= 97 that needs e >= 71 equivalent verdicts (6 by tce, so at least 65 more from the panel), about 37% of stratum A. Exit (b) is therefore effectively decided by the catalog and the panel; the rate is read as a sensitivity measurement, and the per-operator, per-site, per-class, by-language and K1-only rates are the informative outputs.

A.rule: Solidity: every FunctionDefinition and ModifierDefinition the I19 walker reaches from all actions of the adopted extracted rollup document (holon.frontends.solidity.transitions.walk_contract on spec/M2/lib/extract_rollup.json: Collector.reached, the set coverage_document counts for gen/M2/coverage.json; spec/M2/lib/derive_extracted.json adopts the document), plus every function of the header codec libraries (the units of the enc_sol and load_sol edges' op origins: BatchHeaderCodecV0, BatchHeaderCodecV1), OpenZeppelin units included (they compile into Rollup). Go: every function of each Go file that holds the implementation of a CODEC edge or domain predicate of a diagram under gen/M2/diagram/ (the facts' source[].file of those functions with lang go).
A.boundary: Code that reaches an M2 diagram only through TRANS edges built from hand facts (common/batch/batch_data.go, read by L_own_txspayload through spec/M1/facts/morph_batchdata.json and gen/M2/diagram/morph_batchdata.json; it is in stratum B by its codec functions) or that lies outside the adopted extracted rollup document's walk (L1MessageQueueWithGasPriceOracle.sol, which the hand rollup facts cite and no action of the adopted document reaches) is out of stratum A. Stratum A is the adopted extracted document's reach plus the CODEC implementations: a rule that mentions no law, chosen so that A is what the extracted pipeline reads.

B.rule: Every other Go file of the pinned checkout that holds a function a committed spec/M2/facts/*.go.extracted.json lists under go.codecs.encoders, go.codecs.decoders or go.codecs.predicates (I18's codec recognition): extracted but not adopted. Every function of such a file is in scope.

strata.never: No scope or site rule mentions a law, a status or a result.

mstore_offset.pattern: a YulFunctionCall mstore or mstore8 whose first argument is a YulFunctionCall add with two arguments whose second is a decimal YulLiteral K (its source text is decimal digits)
mstore_offset.rewrite: the literal K becomes K-1 (variant -1, only when K >= 1) and K+1 (variant +1)

shl_width.pattern: a YulFunctionCall shl whose first argument is a decimal YulLiteral S
shl_width.rewrite: S becomes S-8 (variant -8) and S+8 (variant +8), each only when 0 < new value < 256

drop_delete.pattern: an ExpressionStatement whose expression is a UnaryOperation delete
drop_delete.rewrite: the statement, from 'delete' through its terminating semicolon, becomes {} followed by the newline characters of the replaced range (variant drop)

swap_cursor.pattern: an Identifier whose referencedDeclaration is a state variable of a pair in cursor_pairs and that is read: not the leftHandSide of an Assignment and not the operand of ++, -- or delete
swap_cursor.rewrite: the identifier becomes the other variable of its pair (variant swap)

cmp_boundary.pattern: a Solidity BinaryOperation with operator >= or > (Yul gt/lt are not matched); the site is the operator token between the operands' source ranges

cmp_boundary_mirror.plan: the mirrored flip of < and <= (new: F-A6)
cmp_boundary_mirror.pattern: a Solidity BinaryOperation with operator <= or <; the site is the operator token

mload_offset.pattern: a YulFunctionCall mload whose first argument is a YulFunctionCall add with two arguments whose second is a decimal YulLiteral K
mload_offset.rewrite: K becomes K-1 (variant -1, only when K >= 1) and K+1 (variant +1)

shr_width.pattern: a YulFunctionCall shr whose first argument is a decimal YulLiteral S
shr_width.rewrite: S becomes S-8 (variant -8) and S+8 (variant +8), each only when 0 < new value < 256

putuint64_offset.pattern: a call binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(x[K:], v): the first argument a slice expression with a decimal integer literal low bound K, no high and no max bound
putuint64_offset.rewrite: K becomes K-1 (variant -1, only when K >= 1) and K+1 (variant +1)

copy_offset.pattern: a call of the builtin copy(x[K:], y): the first argument a slice expression with a decimal integer literal low bound K, no high and no max bound
copy_offset.rewrite: K becomes K-1 (variant -1, only when K >= 1) and K+1 (variant +1)

drop_len_check.pattern: an if statement with no init and no else whose condition is a comparison (==, !=, <, <=, >, >=) of a call len(e) with a decimal integer literal or an identifier declared const in the same file, and whose body is exactly one return statement whose last result is a non-nil error value of the I18 go-errors-nonnil forms: an identifier (or selector) named Err..., errors.New(..) or fmt.Errorf(..)
drop_len_check.rewrite: the statement, from 'if' through its closing brace, becomes {} followed by the newline characters of the replaced range (variant drop)

go_slice_offset.pattern: a slice expression x[K1:K2] with decimal integer literal low and high bounds and no max bound that is read: not the first argument of copy or of a binary.BigEndian.Put* call
go_slice_offset.rewrite: the text K1:K2 becomes K1-1:K2-1 (variant -1, only when K1 >= 1) and K1+1:K2+1 (variant +1): the window moves, its width is kept

roles.doc: The M0 roles a mutant's edges name (projection roles). Solidity: role r is an edge of a mutant iff its function is in walk_functions of r's extracted edge in spec/M2/facts/morph_header.extracted.json (ok_sol is the load_sol edge). Go: role r is an edge iff its function is one of r's functions: the named functions and every function they call transitively through go.calls.edges with callee_kind 'analyzed' in spec/M2/facts/morph_batch.go.extracted.json. m0_law_roles: the functions each laws/M0 statement calls, with ok_go added to every statement that calls dec_go (dec_go is guarded by ok_go). A stratum-B or Rollup-only function has no edge.

M0.decided_by: python -m holon run --milestone M0 --facts <the projected header document> --no-registry

M1x.laws: the 15 laws/M1 laws over spec/M1/facts/morph_rollup.json (L_own_txspayload is over the hand Go facts and has no extracted decision path)
M1x.decided_by: python -m holon differential --milestone M2 (I20) over the mutant's rollup transitions document

M2.laws: laws/M2 as python -m holon derive --milestone M2 re-derives it over the mutant's documents
M2.facts: the documents each law names in 'facts' (spec/M1/facts/morph_rollup.json for SORT-site laws, spec/M2/facts/morph_rollup.extracted.json for SORT-width laws)

law_sets.own_input: A law's own decided input is the sha256 of the canonical JSON {statement, facts, cone}: statement = the law file it is decided from (laws/M0, laws/M1, or the run's laws/M2) with facts_sha256 removed; facts = {path: normalized sha256} of every document it is decided over; cone = {definition: sha256 of its BendTT kernel form} over the model it is decided on (holon.bindings.kernel_cone, the index results/<M>/deps.json is built from). Normalization removes only provenance: a document's top-level 'extraction' block and the 'commit' of its top-level 'target' (a scratch extraction records target.commit null, the frontends' marker for a tree that is not a pinned checkout; the run's source is pinned by mutant_sha256 and preconditions instead). Canonical JSON: json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':')), UTF-8. changed = differs from the baseline record's own input of the same law.
law_sets.carrying: A law whose own decided input equals the baseline's keeps the baseline status (decided: carried): determinism (same statement, facts and kernel forms give the same proof check and the same search). --no-carry decides every law; run --check reruns a sample with --no-carry and a disagreement is an error of the affected laws.
law_sets.matching: A law of a mutant run whose id is absent from the baseline is matched to the baseline law with the same (rule, subform, basis span) when exactly one exists (its record keeps the mutant id under that baseline law); otherwise it is a new law (baseline status 'absent'). Two baseline laws share (SORT, site, morph_rollup:bvh_at), so a re-derived bvh_at law is new (limitations).

predicted.rule: One rule for every operator. predicted(mutant) = M0 laws whose statement calls a role in the mutant's edges (roles.m0_law_roles: dec_go implies ok_go) + M1x laws whose recorded cone (results/M2/extracted_m1/<law>.json 'cone') names one of the mutant's actions (a cone names action a iff it holds the definition step_<a>) + M2 laws whose DERIVATION entry_points include one of the mutant's actions, laws derived only on the mutant included (their entry points read from the mutant run's laws/M2/DERIVATION.json).
predicted.actions: The actions of the adopted rollup document (33, receive included) whose walk reaches the mutant's function: the action's FunctionDefinition and every FunctionDefinition or ModifierDefinition reachable from it through Identifier, IdentifierPath, MemberAccess and ModifierInvocation references in solc 0.8.24's compact AST; their union equals the walker's reached set (computation item 2). Go functions have no action.
predicted.recomputed: Every record also carries its edges, actions and predicted sets recomputed by these rules on the run's own documents (record 'recomputed': {edges, actions, predicted}). The frozen sets decide; an obstruction on a law only the recomputed set predicts is listed under kill_criterion.recomputed_only, never counted.

structural.doc: Which decision paths can see a mutant, from the committed artifacts alone, recorded before freezing so that every survivor is attributed mechanically (the run's survivor class is compared with it and every difference is reported).
structural.projection_read: A site is read by the projection of role r iff (Solidity) its operator is mstore_offset or shl_width and its function is an origin function of an op of an ok path of r (roles.solidity.<r>.origin_functions), or its operator is cmp_boundary or cmp_boundary_mirror and it lies in r's entry function or on a line one of r's revert paths names (roles.solidity.<r>.revert_lines); (Go) its function is one of r's functions. A site in a role's walk that the projection does not read cannot change the projected document: the projection reads ops, lengths and conditions on the role's input, not how the entry function computed the stored values.
structural.M0: reads: some predicted M0 law reads a projection-read site and is PROVED or UNKNOWN at baseline; masked: every such law is REFUTED at baseline; carried: predicted M0 laws exist but none reads a projection-read site; none: no predicted M0 law
structural.M1x: carried: predicted M1x laws exist; they are decided on m1_view, which changes only when a check reach of the same action appears or disappears at an M1 require's span, and no operator here adds or removes one; none: no predicted M1x law
structural.M2: carried: predicted M2 laws exist; SORT-site laws are decided on the hand model (their statement may change through the site: ref, their status cannot), SORT-width laws on the extracted model without a Reach predicate (UNKNOWN only); none: no predicted M2 law

classes.abstraction_carried: M0 is 'none' and M1x or M2 is 'carried'

premise_limited.why: Each keeps the mechanical class 'reachable' (the rule above ignores law premises and argument domains, and stays as it is), but no law that reads it can be killed. A148 and A162 are the +1 copy of SequencerSetVerifyHash at common/batch/batch_header.go:226 and :254: under the ssvh = 0 premise of L_par_hdr_v0 and L_par_hdr_v1 the shifted copy writes the original bytes (byte 217 is overwritten afterwards), and the one law without the premise, L_par_hdr_ssvh, is REFUTED at baseline. A165 to A168 drop length checks of validate() and Version(): L_rt_go_* apply ok_go and dec_go only to enc_sol outputs, which always have the exact length and are never empty, and the one law that sees the change, L_dom_hdr, is REFUTED at baseline.

kill_criterion.plan: A mutant is killed iff the obstruction predicted for its operator appears, localized to the mutated edge: a law moves to REFUTED, with a witness that replays on the mutant code, or a PROVED law loses its proof. A replay disagreement alone is recorded as "extraction defect detected", not as a kill. (BUILD_PLAN I22, verbatim)
kill_criterion.baseline: the same pipeline on the null mutant (the unmutated pinned files in a scratch copy); its statuses and own inputs are the reference
kill_criterion.decided: A law is decided on the mutant by its run's own outcome: REFUTED with a Bend-checked counter-law for its recorded witness is REFUTED, whatever happened to its proof attempt; PROVED is PROVED; UNKNOWN is UNKNOWN unless not_K2 makes it error.
kill_criterion.K1: baseline PROVED or UNKNOWN (or the law is new: absent at baseline, derived on the mutant, its basis span inside a function the mutant mutates), mutant REFUTED with a Bend-checked counter-law for the recorded witness, and the recorded witness replays on the mutant code and does not replay on the original code (replay.hits)
kill_criterion.K2: baseline PROVED, mutant UNKNOWN, and all of: (a) the law's own decided input changed (law_sets.own_input); (b) the generator that proved it at baseline (the baseline record's accepted proof attempt) completed on the mutant and the checker rejected the proof: the attempt's exit_code is not null, the first line of the checker's output (holon.bend's first_line) is 'SOME PROOFS FAIL', and the mutant's generated model module, checked alone (its definitions and no law), gives 'ALL PROOFS CHECK' (proof.model_verdict): the pinned Bend prints 'SOME PROOFS FAIL' for a parse or type error of a generated file too, so only a model that checks alone makes the rejection the proof's (holon.bend's marker alone does not suffice either: it falls back to 'SOME PROOFS FAIL' on any non-zero exit); (c) a code-level localized falsification exists: among the first replay_candidates candidates of the law's deterministic candidate space (refuter order), one makes the claim false on the mutant code and not false on the original code (replay.semantics), or one is a partiality witness (replay.partiality). (a) and (b) without (c): proof_lost_unwitnessed, never a kill. Each K2 records whether its (c) candidate is model_tied (replay.model_tied): reported, not a kill condition.
kill_criterion.not_K2: On the mutant, a timeout of the proof check (exit_code null, '[timeout]'), a checker exit with no verdict line (a crash), a rejection while the generated model alone does not check (a parse or type error of a generated file: proof.model_verdict is not 'ALL PROOFS CHECK'), LG.Unsupported, or a generator returning None is a law-level error (retried once), never K2. It makes the law's mutant status 'error' only for a law PROVED at baseline and decided (run) on the mutant that is neither REFUTED there with a Bend-checked counter-law nor PROVED there (a law that would otherwise end UNKNOWN).
kill_criterion.masked_obstruction: a predicted law REFUTED at baseline one of whose mutant model hits (up to replay_candidates, candidate order) replays on the mutant code and not on the original: reported, never a kill
kill_criterion.replay_disagreement: a law that moves to REFUTED (baseline PROVED, UNKNOWN or new) none of whose hits replays on the mutant code: the model's refutation is not the code's; it sets extraction_defect_detected and is never a kill
kill_criterion.baseline_finding: a law that moves to REFUTED whose hits replay on the mutant code only together with the original (every replaying hit replays on both): a finding the baseline model missed (whitepaper §9.6), never a kill and never an extraction defect
kill_criterion.unpredicted: a law outside the mutant's predicted set that satisfies K1 or K2: recorded per operator, never counted
kill_criterion.recomputed_only: a law outside the frozen predicted set, inside the record's recomputed predicted set, that satisfies K1 or K2: listed per mutant (record 'recomputed_only'), never counted
kill_criterion.killed: some predicted law satisfies K1 or K2 on a decision path that completed
kill_criterion.errors: Errors are scoped to laws. A step that fails for a reason other than the law (an extraction, the projection, a set's run, a proof check that ends without a verdict line, a replay harness build) is retried once; if it fails again it marks as error only the laws it decides, or the law whose witness it replays, and never a law the run decided otherwise (kill_criterion.decided). A failed extraction of a document marks every law whose decision path reads it. outcome = killed if killed; else error if some predicted law is error; else survived. Failures on unpredicted laws and on channels are recorded only. Errors are counted per step. I62 (replaces.defects D4, D5): a set's run (`holon run --milestone M2` over the laws the unit decides) that fails twice is retried law by law, each law alone (twice at most); a law whose own run fails is error, and the laws that pass alone are decided by one run of their own set, as when nothing fails. A channel run that does not complete is retried once (channels.retry).

replay.doc: The replay harness is I61's deliverable, fixed by I62 (replaces.defects D1, D2) (holon/mutate/replay.py, harness sources under replay/M2/mutation_i61/ and, for trace laws, replay/M2/mutation_i62/HolonTraceReplay.t.sol). It evaluates a law's claim, by claim and never by law id, at exact field values, on the code of a given source tree (a mutant's scratch copy or the unmutated one). Its shape comes from the null mutant's documents only (the committed spec/M2/facts at pins.holon_commit); a mutant's own documents never shape its harness.
replay.m0: The statement's IR is evaluated bottom-up; each role call runs on the tree's own implementation. enc_sol runs through a Foundry harness generated for each tree from that tree's own Rollup.sol text. From the null mutant's document (spec/M2/facts/morph_header.extracted.json, functions.enc_sol) it takes the entry function (entry.fn), the lines of the revert paths (paths[].src, outcome revert), the call line of each store op (ops[].origin.stack[0]) with its field map (ops[].src: a Header field, or zeros for a constant) and the call line of the selected sink (sink.stack[0]). From the tree's text it copies, in order: (i) each revert path's require whose path condition, past the conditions of the paths before it, is on the version field alone (the one condition the projection projects: projection.enc_sol), with every occurrence of the version expression read as the witness's version (the version expression is the value argument of the store call whose op's src is the Header field 'version', in the tree's text); (ii) the statements of the innermost block of the entry function that holds every store-op call line and the sink's call line, from its first statement up to the statement holding the sink, with each store call whose op maps a Header field given that field's witness value at the Header field's width (Solidity uint8 for width 1, uint64 for width 8, bytes32 for width 32; I16's abi, replay/M2/implementations.json edges.enc_sol.abi), a store call whose op writes zeros keeping the tree's text, and every occurrence of the version expression read as the witness's version; and (iii) in place of the statement holding the sink, the return of the bytes the sink hashes (its length argument, from its pointer argument, as I16's harness copies them). A local variable the copied statements use that is declared before the block is declared in the harness with its declared type. Revert conditions on other fields are not copied (P-unprojected). ok_sol runs through the tree's Rollup._loadBatchHeader (a subclass, as I16's binding); enc_go_v0, enc_go_v1, ok_go and dec_go through a Go test built in the tree's own package that makes I16's harness's calls (replay/M2/go/holon_codec_test.go, which does not recover) with a recover per call (harness sources under replay/M2/mutation_i61/); view is the specification (facts/morph_header.json functions.view). Each role call runs in a fresh call frame (an external call): memory past the free pointer is zero, as on the deployed path.
replay.hits: The candidates are holon.refute's (holon.refute.candidates with the law's pins) in its order. The model hits are the candidates at which the compiled mutant model shows the claim false with every subterm defined (the refuter's own test), enumerated beyond the first, at most replay_candidates of them. Each is replayed on the mutant tree and on the original tree; the recorded witness is the first hit that replays on the mutant and not on the original, else the first hit. REFUTED needs a Bend-checked counter-law (holon.gen.proofs.counter) for the recorded witness.
replay.semantics: Per the functions' declared meanings (facts/morph_header.json 'meaning'): ok_sol is true iff the loader returns and false on any revert; ok_go is true on a nil error and false on a non-nil one; dec_go is None when validate() errs, else the getters' results in order (a getter that errs after validate() passed is absent, as I16's binding); enc_sol's revert on a copied require has no value. An error or revert that is the function's value is not a violation. A role call with no value, at the top level of the claim or inside another call, makes the candidate no execution (neither falsified nor confirmed: the model's undefined intermediate, holon.refute.subterms). A panic (Go panic, Solidity Panic 0x01-0x51 in a role the meaning gives no revert value) falsifies the claim. Trace laws (M1x, M2): a reverted step is a no-op; a Panic at the law's site falsifies it (the I15 panic_site replay); witnesses replay through holon.mreplay (M1x) and the I15 M2 replay on the tree's Rollup. I62 (replaces.defects D1): a role whose value is none (dec_go's None) is a value: it equals no some(...) value and is compared like any value, so dec_go(x) == some(y) is false where dec_go(x) is none; a field of none, or a role called with none as its argument, is the model's undefined intermediate, no execution.
replay.partiality: A partiality witness of a law (K2 (c)) is a candidate among the first replay_candidates of the law's candidate space that satisfies the law's premises, at which every role call of the claim has a value on the original code and, on the mutant code, some Solidity role call reverts at a line its role names (roles.solidity.<r>.revert_lines) where the original did not revert: the domain of a role the law reads shrank at that candidate. The revert's line is the source line of the reverting require or revert in the tree's text (the harness maps each copied statement back to its line; replay.call reports it as revert_line), and the record keeps the role and the line (falsifier.role, falsifier.revert_line).
replay.model_tied: A K2 (c) candidate is model_tied when, at it, the mutant model's claim is undefined or false and the baseline model's claim is defined and true (both evaluated by holon.refute's own test on the compiled models).
replay.both: a candidate that falsifies the claim on the mutant and on the original code is a baseline finding (kill_criterion.baseline_finding)
replay.trace: I62 (replaces.defects D2): trace laws replay through replay/M2/mutation_i62/HolonTraceReplay.t.sol, I15's trace harness (replay/M1/solidity/HolonTraceReplay.t.sol) with one change: each trace's deployment is first probed from a snapshot that is then reverted, and every step of a trace whose deployment reverts is logged 'rev deploy: <reason>' and not run. No step runs, so none panics at the law's site and the claim holds on that trace. A trace whose deployment succeeds runs as in I15's harness.

harness_gate.doc: A preregistered gate on the replay harness (S-B1 (5)). It runs after the build and before any catalog mutant; if it fails, no catalog mutant runs. `python -m holon mutate gate` writes results/M2/mutation_i62/gate.json; every attempt is kept in it, each at its own pipeline commit, and a fix of holon/mutate after a failed attempt is reported with the attempt it fixes (no catalog mutant has run by then). If an attempt fails for a defect in a tool the rules keep unchanged (an extractor, the M0 pipeline beyond projection.extensions, holon differential, derive or fragments, the I16 or I20 harness), no catalog mutant runs: the defect is reported as a Surprise and the human decides (a fix there reruns everything from scratch).

checks.i16: On the original code, holon.mutate.replay reproduces I16's committed real outputs for every edge (results/M2/refinement/<edge>.json for enc_sol, ok_sol, enc_go_v0, enc_go_v1, ok_go, dec_go: the same compared count and outputs digest on I16's per-edge corpus, `holon mutate replay --i16`).
checks.model: On the original code, for every laws/M0 statement and every candidate of its candidate space (holon.refute.candidates with the law's pins, all of them, in order), every role call whose value in the baseline model (gen/M2/mutation_i62/header.projected.json, compiled by the M0 pipeline) is defined has a harness value equal to it; candidates where the model is undefined are counted, not compared.
checks.null: On the original code, no PROVED M0 law's claim is false at any candidate of its candidate space, and the recorded witness of every REFUTED M0 law (results/M0/<law>.json) makes its claim false.
checks.controls: Each planted control (controls), a fixture outside the catalog, runs through the per-mutant pipeline (`holon mutate run --control <id>`) and is killed through every law its 'expected' names, by the 'how' it names (K1, or K2 with the named falsifier kind). C1 and C2 exercise the codec libraries and the Go encoder, C3 the copied build block of the tree's own entry function (the gap a library-only control leaves: a harness that copied the null tree's entry text would pass C1 and C2), and C4 the copied require with a partiality witness. I62 (replaces.defects D7): a control also fails the check when its record lists a replay disagreement or an error of step 'replay', even when it is killed as expected: the replay harness is what the gate certifies, and I61's C3 record showed the none-value defect (D1) this way before any catalog mutant ran.

controls.why: storeDataHash writes the 32-byte data hash at offset 27 instead of 25: enc_sol differs from enc_go_v0 at every header whose data hash is nonzero, so the re-extracted model refutes L_par_hdr_v0 and its witness replays on the mutated Solidity and not on the original

BatchHeaderV0.Bytes writes the batch index at offset 3 instead of 1: enc_go_v0 differs from enc_sol at every header whose batch index is nonzero, so the re-extracted model refutes L_par_hdr_v0 and its witness replays on the mutated Go and not on the original

inside the copied build block: the header-length selection reads `version >= 3`, so versions 1 and 2 get the 249-byte length; enc_sol of a version-1 header is 249 bytes where enc_go_v1 writes 257, so the re-extracted model refutes L_par_hdr_v1 and its witness replays on the mutated Rollup text (the generated harness runs the tree's own block) and not on the original

the copied version require reads `version <= 0`: every version-1 and version-2 header now reverts, the projected enc_sol is undefined there and the version-1 and version-2 round-trip laws lose their proofs; K2 (c) holds through a partiality witness, a candidate at which the original executes and the mutated require reverts

harness_gate.passed: the gate passed iff every check holds in one attempt, the last, at the records' pipeline_commit
harness_gate.record: results/M2/mutation_i62/gate.json: {"instrument": {"path", "sha256"}, "pipeline_commit", "attempts": [{"pipeline_commit", "checks": {"i16" | "model" | "null" | "controls": {"passed": bool, "detail": str}}, "passed": bool, "fix": null | str}], "passed": bool}; the top-level pipeline_commit is the last attempt's; first committed before any catalog mutant's record.
harness_gate.rehearsal: I62 (replaces.defects D8): no check of the gate (i16, model, null, controls), whole or in part, runs on the build of holon/mutate before the gate's first attempt at the pipeline commit. The gate's attempts are its only runs; a failed attempt is followed by a fix and a new attempt (fix), never by a private rerun.
harness_gate.before_prereg: What the lead ran on the fixed code before this prereg, at local test commits never pushed, with I61's baseline record and inputs (records discarded): the replay of A001's three round-trip laws' 16 hits each on the A001 tree and the original tree (D1: every hit false on the mutant, true on the original); the unit pipeline on A076 (D2) and A116 (D3, D4); and the header-document width law of a kept I61 A116 scratch tree through holon run with the ledger bundle and the coverage rule (UNKNOWN, ledger_match derived). No control and no gate check ran. Before I61's run was merged, the I61 report's diagnostics ran A001 and A058 with a corrected evaluation (docs/iterations/I61.md).

projection.doc: holon/mutate/project.py composes the holon-facts/0.1 header document the 8 laws/M0 statements are decided on, from extracted documents only (I22's projection, kept, with the additions below). types.Header and functions.view are copied from facts/morph_header.json (the laws' binder type and the specification). Every other function comes from its role's extracted document: enc_sol from the enc_sol edge, ok_sol from load_sol, enc_go_v0 and enc_go_v1 from the Go encoders, ok_go from the Go predicate's paths (true exactly where some nil-error path's conditions admit the input; a panicking path is not one), dec_go from the Go decoders guarded by ok_go.
projection.cells: A byte of an integer field written with width w (I17 N1: shl(8k, v) gives w = 32 - k; Go put/copy the field's own width) is aligned big-endian onto the Header field of width W: byte j of the w-byte value is byte W - w + j of the field, and a byte with W - w + j < 0 is the constant 0. A Solidity byte no op writes is undefined (A-dirty); a Go byte no op writes is 0.
projection.enc_sol: the extracted version bound is domain.version_le; per-version length and ops come from the ok paths at each version 0..version_le (length_by_version, ops with when). A revert condition on a field other than the version is not projected (listed in the document's assumptions as P-unprojected:<edge>).
projection.dec_go: each getter comes from its decoder function's nil-error paths (go.functions[fn].paths): one getter per (offset, width) read, with a when from the paths' condition on the version byte (version_ge when the version set is a threshold, else version_in). A getter whose decoder has no nil-error path that reads the input at constant offsets is undefined (every cell undefined).
projection.encoders: an encoder role whose function has no nil-error path (every path panics or errs), or whose cells the extraction leaves unknown, projects to an encoder whose unknown cells are undefined.
projection.extensions: The M0 generator and refuter do not yet accept what the projection needs; the build adds, and only adds: a when {version_in: [...]} on ops and getters, a field cell slice (a field item's from/len), and an undefined cell or getter, to holon/facts.py and holon/gen/model.py, and the matching version and length constants to holon/refute.py's candidate space. Under them facts/morph_header.json compiles to the same bytes and every M0 law decides exactly as before (gate M0 G1 and every results/M0 record unchanged), and no extension adds a top-level definition the ledger bundle does not classify.
projection.output: gen/M2/mutation_i62/header.projected.json is the projection of the committed documents; holon mutate project --check reproduces it.

equivalence.definition: A mutant is equivalent iff, from every state the deployed code can reach, every call sequence through the public entry points gives the same observables on the original and on the mutant. Solidity: the entry points are those of Rollup, the deployed contract that the codec libraries and the inherited OpenZeppelin contracts compile into (the 33 actions of the adopted document, receive included); the observables are the success or revert of each call, its revert data, its return data, the emitted events (topics and data) and every storage slot. Go: the entry points are the exported functions and methods of the mutated package; the observables are the return values, the errors, whether a call panics, and every byte of every slice returned or written. Gas is not an observable. A difference only on states the code cannot reach is no difference. A mutant whose Rollup deployed bytecode equals the original's (tce) is equivalent.
equivalence.contradictions: A verdict 'equivalent' is contradicted when the mutant is killed by K1, has a K2 (c) falsification or partiality witness, has a masked obstruction, or is corpus_detected. A baseline finding is no contradiction (it replays on both trees). Each contradicted verdict is reported as function-level, and also as reachable when the mutant is corpus_detected or the witness of some contradicting law fits an entry point (that law entry's witness_fits_entry): a Go mutant's witness always fits (its package's exported API takes any input); a Solidity mutant's witness fits when every enc_sol call it executes satisfies enc_sol's unprojected revert conditions and every field value fits the extracted Header's value_type, and a witness that executes only the loader fits (the loader reads arbitrary calldata). This approximates reachability under equivalence.definition (states reachable through the public entry points) and is named so: 'reachable (entry-fit)'. rate_non_equivalent is also reported with the function-level and with the reachable contradicted verdicts reversed.

duplicates.rule: Duplicate candidates: the mutants of one statement (the same file and line) that come from two or more sites (any operators), or from one statement-level operator (drop_delete, swap_cursor, cmp_boundary, cmp_boundary_mirror, drop_len_check). The panel decides, for each candidate group, which mutants are semantic duplicates of the group's lowest id (the same observables on every reachable state); the summary reports the rates with each duplicate counted once beside the plain ones.

tce.rule: Trivial compiler equivalence (computation item 6): a Solidity mutant whose Rollup deployed bytecode (solc 0.8.24, optimizer off, cancun, metadata bytecodeHash none, no CBOR) equals the original's. Equivalent by construction; the panel records it so.

channels.doc: Detection channels never decide a kill. Each record lists exactly its runs. Stratum B has none.
channels.i20_step: The baseline and every stratum-A Solidity mutant: I20's step harness (holon fragments with I20's binding replay/M2/fragments.json and --disagreements in scratch) runs the baseline run's corpus (its traces and fork steps) on the mutant contract against the mutant's extracted rollup model. new_disagreements: the disagreements the baseline's run does not have; corpus_differences: the step ids where the mutant contract's observables (status, revert key, touched storage slots, logs) differ from the original contract's on the same corpus. A completed run covers at least 2432 steps (the m1 source alone). I62 (replaces.defects D2): the step harness's Solidity base is replay/M2/mutation_i62/HolonStepBase.sol, I20's replay/M2/solidity/HolonStepBase.sol with one change: each trace's deployment is first probed from a snapshot that is then reverted, and a trace whose deployment reverts writes one line, F <tid> <revert data>, and no other. On the mutant such a trace has no run and its steps are corpus differences (a step id on one side only differs); no step of it is compared, so it has no disagreement and no width observation. The baseline's deployments must all succeed (its run fails otherwise). A trace whose deployment succeeds writes the same lines as under I20's file.
channels.i16_edge: The baseline, every stratum-A Go mutant and every stratum-A Solidity mutant whose edges are non-empty: I16's per-edge refinement of the mutant's projected document against the mutant code on I16's per-edge corpus (new_disagreements as above; corpus_differences null). channels.flags: extraction_defect_detected: true when some law is a replay disagreement or some run reports a new disagreement; null when neither and some run is incomplete; false otherwise. corpus_detected: for a stratum-A Solidity mutant, whether the completed i20_step run's corpus_differences is non-empty; null when that run is incomplete and for every other mutant. A harness that exits without a result (a panic, a build failure) leaves its run incomplete, with its error.

## What the panel decides
For every mutant: is it EQUIVALENT to the original program? Decide from this sheet and the pinned sources alone.
Do not read spec/M2/predictions.json, prompts/I60_mutation_replacement.md, prompts/I61_mutation_second_replacement.md,
tests_m2/test_mutation_adequacy_i60.py, tests_m2/test_mutation_adequacy_i61.py, docs/iterations/I61.md,
docs/iterations/I60_catalog_review.json or any I60 or I61 result: they hold the predictions.
A mutant is equivalent iff, from every state the deployed code can reach, every call sequence through the public
entry points gives the same observables on the original and on the mutant. Solidity: the entry points are those of
Rollup, the deployed contract that the codec libraries and the inherited OpenZeppelin contracts compile into (its
external and public functions and receive); the observables are the success or revert of each call, its revert
data, its return data, the emitted events (topics and data) and every storage slot. Go: the entry points are the
exported functions and methods of the mutated package; the observables are the return values, the errors, whether
a call panics, and every byte of every slice returned or written. Gas is not an observable. A mutant that differs
only on states the code cannot reach is equivalent; one that differs on any reachable state is not. When unsure,
say not equivalent. Every equivalent verdict needs a reason.
These mutants leave Rollup's deployed bytecode unchanged (solc 0.8.24, optimizer off, cancun, no metadata): A110, A111, A112, A113, A121, A122.
They are equivalent by construction.
Duplicate candidates (the mutants of one line from two or more sites, or of one statement-level operator):
For each group, say which mutants give the same observables as the group's lowest id on every reachable state.
The verdicts go to spec/M2/equivalent_mutants_i61.json (the format is in the instrument's "adjudication" field),
committed alone, after the catalog review and before any run. Equivalent mutants leave the denominator of the
non-equivalent kill rate; the rate over all mutants is reported too.
## Operators
- mstore_offset (-1, +1): the literal offset K of an inline-assembly mstore/mstore8(add(p, K), v) becomes K-1 or K+1.
- shl_width (-8, +8): the literal shift S of an inline-assembly shl(S, v) becomes S-8 or S+8.
- drop_delete (drop): a `delete x;` statement becomes the empty block `{}`.
- swap_cursor (swap): a read of lastCommittedBatchIndex becomes lastFinalizedBatchIndex, and vice versa.
- cmp_boundary (flip): a Solidity `>=` becomes `>`, and `>` becomes `>=`.
- cmp_boundary_mirror (flip): a Solidity `<=` becomes `<`, and `<` becomes `<=`.
- mload_offset (-1, +1): the literal offset K of an inline-assembly mload(add(p, K)) becomes K-1 or K+1.
- shr_width (-8, +8): the literal shift S of an inline-assembly shr(S, v) becomes S-8 or S+8.
- putuint64_offset (-1, +1): the literal K of binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(x[K:], v) becomes K-1 or K+1.
- copy_offset (-1, +1): the literal K of copy(x[K:], y) becomes K-1 or K+1.
- drop_len_check (drop): an `if` comparing len(..) with a constant whose body only returns an error becomes `{}`.
- go_slice_offset (-1, +1): a read slice x[K1:K2] with literal bounds becomes x[K1-1:K2-1] or x[K1+1:K2+1].
Every replacement keeps the file's line count, so line numbers in the diffs are the pinned file's.
